title: Quantum Metric Scaling and Its Exceptions in Classical Flat Bands
authors: Kin Hung Fung, K. T. Law, C. T. Chan
abstract: The quantum metric length has been proposed as the localization length scale in one-dimensional flat bands. Here, we study this quantum metric scaling and the exceptions to it in a classical flat band formed by a locally resonant mass--spring system. We find that the localization length follows the quantum metric length near the flat band but departs from this proportionality at the exact flat-band frequency. Selective mass disorder also produces divergent localization lengths or arbitrarily short tails near the flat-band frequency without changing the clean metric. These exceptions show that disorder can select localization scales beyond those predicted by the quantum metric alone.
summary: This paper analyzes how disorder affects the localization length in flat-band systems modeled by a mass-spring chain. It shows that while the localization length usually scales predictably with the quantum metric, specific types of disorder at the exact flat-band frequency cause deviations. These exceptions reveal that disorder can select localization scales beyond what the quantum metric alone predicts.
main_problem: The study investigates the quantum metric scaling of localization length in classical flat bands and identifies specific exceptions to this scaling law.
main_result: While the localization length generally follows the quantum metric length near the flat band, selective mass disorder at the exact flat-band frequency causes deviations, suggesting the quantum metric sets a minimum localization scale.
method: The analysis uses the Bloch equation for a locally resonant mass-spring chain, incorporating mass disorder, and compares the calculated localization length ($\xi$) against the quantum metric length ($\ell_{QM}$).
model_or_system: The system is a locally resonant mass–spring chain modeled by a Hamiltonian leading to the Bloch equation $D(k)U = \omega^2MU$. Disorder is introduced via random mass loading ($m_{\alpha,n} = m_{\alpha}(1 + W b_{\alpha,n})$).
key_observables: Localization length ($\xi$), Quantum Metric Length ($\ell_{QM}$), and the ratio $\xi/\ell_{QM}$.
important_parameters: Gap-opening parameter ($\delta$), Disorder Strength ($W$), and Detuning ($\eta$ or $b_\epsilon$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the model of the locally resonant mass–spring chain and treats the mass disorder as independent random loading.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate quantum metric localization near the flat band under disorder, showing crossovers between conventional scaling and the plateau set by $\ell_{QM}$. Comparisons are made between $\xi/\ell_{QM}$ at the exact flat-band frequency versus detuned frequencies.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the quantum metric concept, analyzes the localization length ($\xi$) in the presence of disorder, details the general quantum metric scaling, and then focuses on the specific, anomalous scaling laws observed at the exact flat-band frequency due to selective disorder coupling.
why_interesting: The work provides a detailed theoretical understanding of how geometric invariants (like the quantum metric) govern transport properties in engineered systems, while also pinpointing the precise conditions (selective disorder) where these predictions break down, which is crucial for designing robust quantum devices.
